text.p: Following are the main stories in Slovenia's Friday morning newspapers.
- The government designed a programme that would prevent unregistered employment, which represents 25 percent of Slovenia's GDP.
- The Pension Fund said pensions will be raised by 1.2 percent from August.
- Marko Milic became the first Slovenian basketball player to join the NBA league after signing a contract with Philadelphia 76-ers on Thursday.
- Slovenian tourist officials said there were nine percent more hotel guests at the Slovenian seaside this week than at the same time last year.
- Television advertising rose six percent in the first half of 1996, a media research showed.
- The Ministry of Transport said it would spend 59 billion tolars on highway construction this year ($361 million).

- About 48.4 percent of Slovenians watched private television POP TV at least 15 minutes per day in the first six months of this year compared to 53.3 percent that spend at least a quarter of an hour per day watching national television channel TV Slovenija.
- The parliamentary board of finance and monetary policy supported the new bill on foreign exchange transactions.
- The decree according to which salaries of employees in public institutions could be publicly revealed expired in June.
- The Ministry of Finance will sell three-year six percent bonds which will be issued on July 23 to 12 Slovenian banks out of the 14 that participated in this week's auction.
